The '''2025–26 Ligue 1''', also known as '''Ligue 1 [[McDonald's France|McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 88th season of the [[Ligue 1]], France's premier football competition.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5359153/2024/03/21/mcdonalds-ligue-1-sponsor/ |title=French football league to be rebranded as Ligue 1 McDonald's from next season |work=The New York Times |access-date=12 May 2025 |last1=Rutzler |first1=Peter |date=21 March 2024 |archive-date=20 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520091533/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5359153/2024/03/21/mcdonalds-ligue-1-sponsor/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It began on 15 August 2025 and concluded on 17 May 2026. The match schedule was announced on 27 June 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ligue1.fr/articles/l1_article_2032-les-grandes-dates-de-la-saison-2025-26-l1|title=Les grandes dates de la saison 2025/26 !|date=27 February 2025|publisher=Ligue 1|access-date=12 May 2025|archive-date=18 July 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250718211011/https://ligue1.fr/articles/l1_article_2032-les-grandes-dates-de-la-saison-2025-26-l1|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the four-time defending champions,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp6gyyr372zo|title=PSG clinch Ligue 1 title after Monaco beaten|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 April 2024|access-date=28 April 2024|archive-date=19 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719134935/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp6gyyr372zo|url-status=live}}</ref> and successfully defended the title, mathematically securing a record-extending fourteenth title, and their fifth consecutive title, with one match to spare on 13 May 2026, following a 2–0 win against closest competitors [[RC Lens|Lens]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48756809/psg-lens-ligue-1-title-france-champions-record-luis-enrique|title=PSG beat Lens to clinch 5th straight Ligue 1 title|publisher=ESPN|date=13 May 2026|access-date=13 May 2026|archive-date=15 May 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260515050847/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48756809/psg-lens-ligue-1-title-france-champions-record-luis-enrique|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Teams ==
A total of eighteen teams participated in the 2025–26 edition of the Ligue 1. [[FC Lorient|Lorient]], [[Paris FC]], and [[FC Metz|Metz]] were promoted after finishing first, second, and winning the play-off final in the [[2024–25 Ligue 2]], respectively. Both Lorient and Metz returned to the top flight after one year's absence, while Paris FC returned to the top flight after a forty-six year's absence. They replaced [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] (relegated after sixteen years in the top flight), [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] (relegated after one year in the top flight), and [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] (relegated after seven years in the top flight).

==Relegation play-offs==
The 2025–26 season concluded with a relegation play-off between the 16th-placed Ligue 1 team, [[OGC Nice|Nice]], and the winner of the semi-final of the [[2025–26 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]] play-off, [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]], in a two-legged confrontation.
